headline: Revenue grows but margins compress as outlook is trimmed
summary_short: Lululemon's fiscal Q1 2026 revenue rose 4.3% y/y to $2.472 billion, but gross margin fell 410bp to 54.2% and operating income dropped 36.9% to $276.9 million as diluted EPS fell to $1.69 from $2.60.
summary_long: Revenue rose 4.3% y/y to $2.472 billion (+2% constant currency), with International up 22% (+16% cc) offsetting a 3% Americas decline; comparable sales were +1% (-2% cc), split -5% Americas vs +13% international. Gross margin fell 410bp to 54.2% and operating margin fell 730bp to 11.2% as SG&A rose to 42.9% of revenue from 39.8%; operating income fell 36.9% to $276.9 million and diluted EPS fell to $1.69 from $2.60. Net income was $195.0 million, down 38.0%. The company repurchased $358.3 million of stock and ended the quarter with $1.51 billion in cash. Citing demand headwinds, management lowered its full-year outlook to $11.00-$11.15 billion revenue and $10.95-$11.15 diluted EPS, and guided Q2 revenue to $2.450-$2.475 billion and EPS to $1.76-$1.81.

drivers.explanation: International net revenue grew 22% (16% cc) driven by China Mainland (+30%/+23% cc) and Rest of World, offsetting a 3% (4% cc) Americas decline.
Operating margin compression (-730bp) exceeds gross-margin compression (-410bp), implying most of the extra decline came from SG&A deleverage (42.9% of revenue vs 39.8% a year ago).
Not explained in the release beyond the reported 410bp margin decline; no specific cause (freight, promotions, tariffs) is attributed.
Management cited demand headwinds requiring 'additional actions to reposition' the business and adjusted the full-year outlook downward.
